latencies.notes: Data-dependent. Same classes as the LSX form, with two quotient bits per cycle instead of four: 11 for 0, Inf or NaN inputs; 13 when the quotient overflows or underflows; 15 when the quotient is exact; 17 for an exact quotient with a subnormal operand; 25 when the inexact quotient is tiny (1.0/max); 27 when the quotient needs the full 23-bit mantissa; 29 with a subnormal operand. Long path: 15 + 2*ceil(23/4) = 27, so the vector single-precision divide is slower than the scalar one even though both doubles match.

throughput.notes: Throughput range over 22 operand values: min CPI 4.50 at 1/0, max CPI 13.50 at 1/maxsub. Sample uses 1/1.

notes: LASX variable-latency floating-point instruction. Latency measured with a reset helper that keeps element 0 at the test value; throughput measured with 8 independent lanes. Ranges cover special values, exact/non-exact cases, subnormals, and overflow/underflow boundaries. Both vector sources are recorded separately; they share the same result path where the hardware is symmetric.
